PullRequest.Title: sessions: Reopen dismissed canvases from Add Tab
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- Add live dismissed canvases to the Agents Window editor's Add Tab menu.
- Scope entries to the active session and chat, and reopen the exact selected canvas instance.
- Use provider titles and semantic instance IDs with collision-safe fallback labels.
- Preserve stable menu command identities across metadata updates and recover dismissal state from failed editor opens.
- Document the reopen workflow in Canvas Accessibility Help.

## Testing

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/test/electron-browser/sessionCanvasService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/test/common/sessionCanvas.test.ts` — passed, 15 tests.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/common/sessionCanvas.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/electron-browser/sessionCanvasActions.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/electron-browser/sessionCanvasService.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/test/electron-browser/sessionCanvasService.test.ts` — passed.
- Code OSS Dev on macOS — passed: opened two agent-owned instances, dismissed both, verified titled Add Tab entries, and reopened the selected instance.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents Window startup and active-chat canvas observation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The BlockRestore contribution synchronously creates the existing canvas service and the new menu autorun. It performs bounded in-memory derivation/registration; remote canvas subscriptions may begin asynchronously through the already-observed active chat state and are not newly required by the menu observer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to active chat state and up to eight canvas-state channels through the agent-host connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One chat subscription plus at most eight canvas subscriptions for the active chat, shared/retained by the connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: SessionCanvasService's existing autorun already read activeChat.canvases, activating the same subscription graph before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Subscription setup supplies live state but is not awaited by the synchronous menu-registration path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active chat, one chat-state subscription, and up to eight projected canvases (MAX_PROJECTED_CANVASES = 8). Dismissed history can span chats, but the pre-existing service already scans that same map on active canvas changes; the added bounded menu projection did not establish a realistic material regression.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One observable graph per service; provider subscriptions are retained/shared by connection.getSubscription. Menu registry notifications are microtask-coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider structurally deduplicates canvas membership, caches mapped per-canvas observables, and shares retained state subscriptions. The new derived value reuses those observables and does not create a parallel cache or subscription.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the pre-existing service autorun and provider observable construction directly establish subscription reuse and the eight-canvas cap.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact subscription transport latency is provider-dependent, but no additional subscription cardinality is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: startup adds only small bounded in-memory menu bookkeeping and reuses pre-existing remote observations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dismiss a live canvas and keep its Add Tab entry synchronized with provider metadata
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Input disposal synchronously records one dismissed reference, invalidates the derived list, computes labels for at most eight active-chat canvases, and registers or updates menu items. Provider metadata updates rerun this in-memory projection; unchanged title/order values avoid menu re-registration.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most eight active-chat canvas entries. Inactive dismissed references may remain in the pre-existing map, but realistic update work is bounded by the service's existing lifecycle and the provider cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable invalidations are transactional. Menu changes are emitted through a MicrotaskEmitter, coalescing multiple registration changes in one turn.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Registrations are keyed by stable canvas reference and reused across metadata changes; unchanged labels/orders are skipped. Removed entries dispose both command and menu registration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: stable-key reuse, disposal, update guards, the provider cap, and microtask coalescing are explicit in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A long-lived service can hold dismissed references across chats, but each chat has at most eight canvases and the diff does not create unbounded command/menu retention.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: CPU/allocation work is small and bounded, menu updates are coalesced, and lifecycle cleanup is present.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reopen one dismissed canvas from the Add Tab menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selected command removes its dismissed/menu state, opens one editor, creates one external BrowserView over IPC, and loads its HTTP(S) URL before the canvas is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an external BrowserView in the main process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getOrCreateBrowserView IPC call per explicit reopen.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A dismissed canvas could not be reopened manually, so this explicit user-triggered boundary did not exist; initial automatic presentation already used the same editor/browser-view path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited on the user-triggered reopen path before the editor can present the view.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the selected canvas HTTP(S) source in the BrowserView.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No manual reopen was available after dismissal; the same single navigation occurred for initial automatic canvas presentation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the reopened canvas is displayed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one selected canvas per command invocation; the dismissed item is synchronously removed, preventing the same menu action from remaining active during the open.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One open promise for the selected command. Different canvases could be selected independently, but the UI exposes at most eight and the diff introduces no bulk fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reopening creates a fresh ephemeral BrowserView because closing disposed the prior input/model; there is no warm browser-view cache to reuse. Canvas state itself comes from the existing live provider subscription.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the command-to-editor-to-BrowserView call path and both awaited boundaries are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Page load duration depends on the selected source, but cardinality is one and directly user-requested.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new IPC/network work is the requested operation, has cardinality one, and is not eagerly or repeatedly triggered.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automatic reveal failure, session/chat switch, and dismissed-entry cleanup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Automatic reveal still performs one editor open as before. On failure, the diff records a reopenable entry in memory; switching/removing ownership deletes entries and disposes their dynamic commands/menu registrations. Existing editor closure remains asynchronous and unchanged in cardinality.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open/close editor and create/destroy its BrowserView as applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open per newly published canvas or explicit reopen; existing close cardinality is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Automatic reveal and ownership cleanup already opened/closed the same editor resources; the refactor adds failure bookkeeping but no extra automatic open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Automatic reveal is off the caller's critical path; explicit reopen awaits completion. Cleanup closes are asynchronous.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most eight current-chat canvases plus retained dismissed references from prior chats/sessions; removals are synchronous per reference and menu events are coalesced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Automatic opens remain independently initiated per newly published canvas, capped at eight by the provider. This PR does not increase that fan-out; it centralizes the same open call in _openInput.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Failed opens become a negative/reopenable state rather than being retried automatically. Successful reopen removes the state; failed reopen restores it only while the input is still live and enabled.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: _presented/_dismissed transitions and the unchanged automatic autorun call site establish the scheduling and cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure frequency and provider behavior vary, but the changed state prevents retry loops rather than creating them.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: failure handling does not retry expensive work, cleanup disposes registrations, and automatic boundary count is unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all six changed files. Traced startup observation, provider updates, menu registration lifecycle, manual reopen, failure recovery, and session cleanup through network/IPC boundaries. The new work is bounded by an eight-canvas provider cap, reuses existing subscriptions, coalesces menu notifications, and performs expensive BrowserView creation/navigation only once per explicit user reopen; no high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.
